entities.summary:
Guy of Anderlecht, also known as Saint Guidon, was a Christian saint venerated in Catholic and Orthodox churches. He was born in the early 11th century and died on September 18, 1012, in Anderlecht, near present-day Brussels, Belgium. The Poor Man of Anderlecht was known for his charitable works and his devotion to the poor, and his legacy has endured for centuries. His feast day is still celebrated in many churches, and he is remembered as a symbol of compassion and generosity. 

 Guy of Anderlecht's life was marked by his dedication to the poor and the marginalized. He was particularly drawn to the sick and the abandoned, and he spent much of his time caring for the poor and the vulnerable. His charitable works took him to various parts of Europe, where he brought hope and comfort to those in need.

 The legacy of Guy of Anderlecht can be seen in the many institutions and charities that bear his name. The Saint Guidon Institute in Belgium, the Saint Guidon Foundation in France, and the Guidon House in Ireland are just a few examples of the many organizations that have been established in his honor. These institutions continue to carry out the work of the Poor Man of Anderlecht, providing aid and support to those in need.

 Guy of Anderlecht's story is also closely tied to the history of the Crusades. He was a devout Christian who believed in the importance of defending the faith, and he played a significant role in the early years of the Crusades. He traveled to the Holy Land, where he fought alongside other Crusaders and helped to establish Christian settlements. His experiences during the Crusades had a profound impact on his life and his work, and he returned to Europe with a renewed sense of purpose and a deeper commitment to the poor and the marginalized.
